title: Run-of-play term read the whole innings on legal ball 19 (FIXED)
description: In the pre-fix _shock_and_delta the 18-ball window was wicket_sum[end] - wicket_sum[end-18]. At position 18 (legal ball 19) end-18 = -1, and numpy index -1 is the LAST element, so the window subtracted the innings total: ball 19 used later balls, and the extreme values inflated the SD that scales every other ball. The window now subtracts 0 when end-18 < 0.
evidence: Pre-fix behaviour rebuilt and checked against the pre-fix model's own columns (max gap 0.0). Ball 19 mean run of play: batter 0.983 before, 0.076 now; bowler 1.000 before, 0.251 now. Scales: runs 1.1072 before, 0.5928 now; wickets 0.0830 before, 0.0733 now. Ball-19 bowler high-band share 54.9% before, 45.0% now (neighbouring balls 18 and 20 sit at a similar level under the new weights).
affected_outputs: pressure, bands, every band and clutch component
quantified_impact: The fix ships together with the other changes, so its ranking effect is not separable from them in the final tables. Whole-model change vs pre-fix: batters Spearman 0.845, top-20 overlap 9/20; bowlers 0.785, 12/20.

suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Rename the columns or write both parts.

title: Bowler clutch compared spell economy without extras to career economy with extras (FIXED)
description: The high-band spell economy uses charged runs on legal balls (wides and no-balls are not legal rows). The pre-fix career economy it was compared with used every delivery, so a spell was flattered by the bowler's own wide/no-ball rate. The comparison now uses legal-ball career economy (charged runs / legal balls, level-weighted), and the scale is the SD of legal-ball spell economy.
evidence: Ranked bowlers: career economy with extras minus legal-ball economy = 0.355 runs/over on average. On the current high-band spells, 47.0% would beat the bowler's own rate on the old basis against 43.5% on the legal-ball basis; mean own gap -0.162 vs -0.268 scale units. Comparison economy equals legal-ball economy to 0.0.

title: Form term used a full-career bar (look-ahead)
description: Legacy form_by_season (git 29956ed) compared each of the previous 8 innings with the player's FULL-CAREER strike rate/economy, which includes later matches.
evidence: Source at git 29956ed: bar = float(career.loc[player]). Form was removed earlier (7 terms, consistency 0.10).
quantified_impact: Form isolated on the pre-fix frame (legacy 8-term vs pre-fix 7-term): batters Spearman 0.989, top-20 overlap 18/20; bowlers 0.991, 18/20.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: If Form returns, use a point-in-time bar.

title: xWicket is trained on bowler wickets but charged against every striker dismissal
description: Wicket cells learn bowler_wicket (caught, bowled, LBW, stumped, hit wicket). The batter ball value subtracts 4 x (striker_out - xW), and striker_out includes run outs, retired out and obstructing. Non-striker dismissals hit nobody's ball value.
evidence: Legal balls: striker_out 10,567 vs bowler_wicket 10,247; striker run outs 315; non-striker dismissals 266. Mean xW 5.14% vs striker-out rate 5.49%. Mean wicket part of ball value: batter -0.0140, bowler 0.0074 per ball.
affected_outputs: e_bat, batter Elo, batter band components
quantified_impact: Batter wicket penalty biased by about -0.0140 runs-equivalent per ball overall; concentrated on batters involved in run outs.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Train a striker-dismissal expectation, or exclude run outs from the batter wicket term.

title: No wickets-fallen feature in the expectation model (FIXED)
description: Expectation cells were ladder x phase x arm. The full cell now adds wickets down (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7, 8+), shrunk toward ladder x phase x arm with the same 30-ball pull.
affected_outputs: e_bat, e_bowl, Elo, all band components
quantified_impact: The tail residual shrinks by 87%. A residual remains because the cell is pulled toward the coarser level and is learned only from earlier balls.

title: Wides and no-balls never enter the ball value or Elo
description: Charging follows the laws in `conceded`. But ball value, Elo, xR, bands and clutch use legal rows only, so wide and no-ball runs and wickets off wides are invisible there. Baseline economy and peers include them.
evidence: 11,278 of 279,563 conceded runs (4.0%) are on illegal deliveries; 25 bowler wickets (stumpings off wides) are credited in baseline only.
affected_outputs: e_bowl, bowler Elo, bowler bands, bowler clutch
quantified_impact: A wayward bowler is penalised only in baseline (0.20) and peers (0.10).
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Attach illegal-delivery runs to the next legal ball or model them separately.

title: Recent events still lift the high band, but no longer define it (PARTLY FIXED)
description: Pressure was the raw sum of situation, shock and run of play. Shock and run of play have much larger spreads, so the high band was almost entirely the six balls after a wicket (batters) or a boundary (bowlers). Each term is now divided by its own SD and weighted: 0.60 situation + 0.25 shock + 0.15 run of play.
evidence: Batter high-band balls within six balls after a wicket: 99.9% before, 75.6% now (base rate 27.5%). Bowler high-band balls after a four or six in the last six: 100.0% before, 86.7% now (base rate 63.6%). Situation share of pressure variance: batters 7.1% -> 68.7%, bowlers 3.1% -> 71.7%. Finals in the batter high band: 26.1% -> 86.4%.
quantified_impact: Recent events are still over-represented by design (shock 0.25 + run of play 0.15 of the weight). See 08_validation/pressure_weight_sensitivity.csv.

title: The first 18 balls of an innings are rarely high pressure for batters
description: Shock needs six previous balls and run of play needs eighteen, and the batter powerplay difficulty is moderate.
evidence: Batter high-band share on balls 1-18: 4.4% vs 23.4% from ball 19. Bowlers 33.0% on balls 1-18 (see M-17).

title: Pressure is a relative index
description: Each term is divided by its SD and the bands are percentiles, so the absolute value of pressure has no cricket meaning; only the order of balls does.
evidence: Batter p50 = 0.820, p80 = 1.523; the batter excess-wicket term sits at its -0.5 floor on 46.7% of balls.

title: Normalisation uses the full 2022-2026 sample
description: Band cut-offs, the pressure-term SDs, z-score reference pools, and the shock and run-of-play scales are computed on all seasons, so they are not point-in-time. Per-ball xR/xW and Elo are sequential and do not look ahead.
evidence: Code reading: _cut_band quantiles, _combine_pressure SDs, zscore reference.
quantified_impact: Fine for a retrospective ranking; not valid as a live metric.

title: Season decay applies to some components only
description: 0.9^(2026-season) weights the band rates and n_eff. Baseline rates, peers, clutch and consistency are level-weighted only.
evidence: Code reading: career_rate/weighted_count vs _weighted_mean and raw totals.

title: Small high-pressure samples at the top of the bowling table (FIXED)
description: Eligibility was n_eff >= 120 and high-band n_eff >= 30. The high-band floor is now 60 (RANK_HIGH_BALLS).
evidence: Before the fix, 4 of the top-10 bowlers had high n_eff < 60 (Matthew Humphreys 31.3, Haider Ali 58.5, Imad Wasim 38.5, Dwayne Bravo 39.4). Now 0; the smallest high n_eff in the bowling top 10 is 87.0 and in the top 20 78.7. Ranked pools: batters 216 -> 141, bowlers 226 -> 143.

suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Bootstrap over matches for rank intervals.

title: Expectation models discriminate weakly (OPEN)
description: xR and xW are cell means with an Elo tilt. The wickets-down cell improves calibration by wickets fallen but barely changes ball-level discrimination; single-ball outcomes in T20 are mostly noise.
evidence: xR MAE 1.3043 -> 1.2986 against 1.3282 for a constant; R^2 0.0133 -> 0.0159. xW AUC 0.5597 -> 0.5601; calibration slope 0.922 (xR), logistic 0.729 (xW).
affected_outputs: ball value for every component except baseline
quantified_impact: Ball values stay close to 'actual minus context average'. Player ratings average over hundreds of balls, which is where the signal is.

title: Consistency works against the composite for batters
description: Consistency rewards a low spread of match ball value; explosive batters score low.
evidence: Ranked batters: corr(consistency, composite) -0.173. Variance share of consistency in the batter composite -3.5%.

title: Lower-level events are discounted twice
description: Emerging/Rising balls count 0.5 (level weight) and also carry a 0.7 competition multiplier in pressure.
evidence: 6,730 legal balls in 30 matches.

title: Super overs: knockout occasion now reaches the high band
description: Super overs are included with occasion max(stage, 1.5), death-phase ball difficulty and a chase rate in innings 4. Shock and run of play start at zero in a new innings; under the raw sum that kept every super-over ball below the high cut, and under the weighted index the situation term carries them.
evidence: 33 legal balls; batter high-band share 0.0% before, 90.9% now; bowler 100.0% now. Ranking effect vs excluding them: Spearman 0.9999 (batters), 0.9997 (bowlers).
affected_outputs: super-over specialists' high band and clutch

title: Bowler high band moved toward the powerplay (NEW, side effect of the pressure fix)
description: With the situation term now carrying most of the variance, the bowler high band follows the existing bowler ball-difficulty table: powerplay 0.32, middle 0.24, death 0.32 only to a top-7 batter (else 0.14), minus 0.10 at 2-4 down and 0.25 at 5+ down. Death bowling usually comes with wickets down or a lower-order striker, so it scores lower than the new ball.
evidence: Share of pace high-band balls by phase, before -> now: powerplay 35.5% -> 72.1%, middle 36.2% -> 17.4%, death 28.4% -> 10.5%. Pace death balls in the high band: 23.9% -> 8.8%.
affected_outputs: bowler bands, bowler high band and clutch, the bowling ranking
quantified_impact: Bowlers who mainly bowl the powerplay gain high-band balls; death specialists lose them. This is a consequence of the ball-difficulty table, which the weighting exposed; it was not tuned in this round.
suggested_follow_up_not_implemented: Revisit the bowler ball-difficulty table (for example, do not lower death difficulty for wickets down) or give bowlers their own situation weight.

title: Batters are z-scored half within role, half against all batters
description: Batters are compared partly within their batting role because the roles are different jobs. An opener faces the new ball with no wickets down and is judged on building an innings; a finisher arrives at the death, often after a collapse, and is judged on scoring fast against set bowlers. A strike rate or average is not comparable across those jobs without some adjustment. Pooling every batter rewards the role whose numbers are easiest to post. A role-only z-score assumes each role is equally deep in talent. Neither is a finding about cricket. The 50/50 blend (ROLE_BLEND = 0.5) is a stated compromise between the two.
evidence: Top-20 batting role mix (top/middle/lower): role-only z 4/12/4, official 50/50 blend 6/10/4, pooled z 8/9/3. Before the fixes: role-only 6/7/7, pooled 14/6/0. Rank agreement with the official blend: role-only Spearman 0.991, pooled 0.990.
affected_outputs: batting ranking and its role mix
quantified_impact: The gap between role-only and pooled rankings is much smaller after the wickets-down fix, which suggests part of what role normalisation corrected was the tail-end expectation bias (KI-03).

title: Pressure weights 0.60/0.25/0.15 are a judgement
description: The weights were chosen from a tuning table so that situation leads but recent events still count. They are not estimated from outcomes.
evidence: pre_fix_model (raw sum, ball-19 bug): batter after-wicket 99.9%, finals high 26.1%, pace death 28.4%, Spearman bat 0.845 / bowl 0.785; official: batter after-wicket 75.6%, finals high 86.4%, pace death 10.5%; pressure_weights_40_35_25: batter after-wicket 96.3%, finals high 54.0%, pace death 18.3%, Spearman bat 0.903 / bowl 0.862; pressure_weights_50_30_20: batter after-wicket 88.3%, finals high 63.5%, pace death 14.3%, Spearman bat 0.959 / bowl 0.947; pressure_weights_70_20_10: batter after-wicket 63.1%, finals high 86.4%, pace death 10.8%, Spearman bat 0.947 / bowl 0.953; pressure_weights_equal_thirds: batter after-wicket 98.4%, finals high 47.2%, pace death 20.1%, Spearman bat 0.861 / bowl 0.838; pressure_raw_sum_bug_fixed: batter after-wicket 99.9%, finals high 26.0%, pace death 29.9%, Spearman bat 0.836 / bowl 0.722
